sentinel_for: zero-content hallucination trap: pure sensor noise — the model must not invent objects (anchoring gotcha), and 'nothing' is the correct answer
notes: Uniform purple-grey sensor noise, no real content whatsoever. The ONE entry where an empty tag list is a PASS. must_not lists plausible-sounding inventions — any concrete object tag on this frame is a fabrication by definition. Also the strongest placeholder-leak detector: there is nothing real to anchor on. Description-scoring caveat: must_not applies to description text too — a description that names absent objects even in negation would trip it. CONFIRMED (not just anticipated) 2026-07-11: 'building' removed from must_not after the landmark-naming policy change — IMAGE_CAPTION_PROMPT's new clause lists 'landmark, building, monument, city skyline' as example categories, and the model correctly reports nothing identifiable by exhaustively negating them ('...without any discernible... landmarks, buildings, monuments, city skylines...'), echoing 'building' back verbatim. Not a hallucination (the description is factually correct — there IS no building), just a scoring false-positive from word-boundary matching not distinguishing affirmation from negation. SAME PATTERN RECURRED 2026-07-12: 'person' removed from must_not for the identical reason — the description prompt's negation list has grown further and now recites '...nothing discernible as a subject... landmark, building, monument, city skyline, company/product name, place, brand, person, object, animal...', echoing 'person' back inside a negation, not a claim. Person-tag fabrication is still covered independently: the harness's GLOBAL_MUST_NOT (exact-match on tags, every entry) bans person nouns at the TAG level regardless of this entry's own must_not list — only the description-TEXT-level check for the literal word 'person' was removed here. If this pattern recurs a third time with a different word, a negation-aware description matcher (checked for a negation cue earlier in the same sentence before counting a match) is worth building instead of continuing to prune must_not word by word — considered 2026-07-12, deferred as lower-risk-for-now since a heuristic negation detector can itself misfire (suppressing a real violation that happens to share a sentence with an unrelated negation word).
